title: Inverse matrices preserve shifted degree-lex coefficient support
statement:
Let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field], $m,n,r\ge0$, and $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in\mathbf N^n$. On $\mathbf N^{m+n}$ use ascending lexicographic order of $(|\alpha|,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_{m+n})$, with the first $m$ coordinates before the last $n$. Let $A=(A_{ij})$ be an $r\times r$ matrix [def-weil-matrix] over $L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and use the determinant of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Suppose $\det(A)(0)\ne0$, and suppose for every $i,j$ and $\delta\in\mathbf N^m$,
$$[W^\delta]A_{ij}\ne0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad(\delta,u_i)\ge(0,u_j).$$
Then $A$ has a unique two-sided inverse over $L[[W]]$, and for every $i,j,\delta$ its entries satisfy
$$[W^\delta](A^{-1})_{ij}\ne0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad(\delta,u_i)\ge(0,u_j).$$
The assertion includes repeated weights, no $W$ variables, and the empty matrix.

source.place: Agent algebra refinement of the local coefficient construction on the ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 route. Motivating finite matrix solve: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 9.12 and (9.13), printed pp.280--281, online journal PDF https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf . ILO does not state this support estimate; a complete cofactor argument is recorded in report.md. No single Stacks tag states it.

proof.text:
Write $R=L[[W]]$. Extend the exponent comparison to the lexicographically ordered abelian group $G=\mathbf Z^{1+m+n}$ by the additive map
$$\theta(\delta,v)=(\sum_a\delta_a+\sum_bv_b,\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_m,v_1,\ldots,v_n).$$
For nonnegative exponents this is exactly the order in the statement. Translation preserves and reflects lexicographic comparisons: the first unequal coordinate is unchanged on adding the same vector. Sums of nonnegative vectors in this order are nonnegative: at the earliest coordinate where any summand is nonzero, every such summand is positive. Thus finitely many weak inequalities can be added and common vectors cancelled. Also $\theta(\epsilon,0)\ge0$ for $\epsilon\in\mathbf N^m$, since either $\epsilon=0$ or its total degree is positive.

proof.text: Put $D=\det A$. The field definition makes $D(0)\ne0$ a unit of $L$; a field is a local ring with maximal ideal zero. By clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring], $D$ is a unit of $R$; choose its scalar inverse $h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity], the matrix $B=h\operatorname{adj}(A)$ satisfies $AB=BA=1$, since $hD=1$ and scalar multiplication commutes with matrix multiplication over the commutative ring $R$. If $B'$ is another two-sided inverse, $B'=B'(AB)=(B'A)B=B$. It remains to check the coefficients of this explicit $B$.

proof.text: Suppose $r>0$, and fix $i,j$. By the cofactor description in [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity], $\operatorname{adj}(A)_{ij}$ is, up to sign, the determinant with row $j$ and column $i$ deleted. Expand this determinant by [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] and its products by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. A nonzero coefficient at $W^\delta$ has a nonzero summand in these finite sums. Such a summand chooses a bijection $\sigma:I\setminus\{j\}\to I\setminus\{i\}$, where $I=\{1,\ldots,r\}$, and exponents $\delta_k\in\mathbf N^m$ with $\sum_{k\ne j}\delta_k=\delta$, such that every $[W^{\delta_k}]A_{k,\sigma(k)}$ is nonzero. Indeed a nonzero product cannot have a zero factor. Each coefficient sum is finite because there are finitely many decompositions of the fixed nonnegative multi-index $\delta$. The empty product for $r=1$ contributes only at $\delta=0$.

proof.text:
For the summand in step 3, the given support condition reads $\theta(\delta_k,u_k)\ge\theta(0,u_{\sigma(k)})$ for every $k\ne j$. Set $U=\sum_{k\in I}u_k$. Add these inequalities using step 1. The bijection exhausts precisely the columns other than $i$, so
$$\theta(\delta,U-u_j)\ge\theta(0,U-u_i).$$
Add $\theta(0,u_i+u_j)$ and cancel $\theta(0,U)$ in $G$. This gives $\theta(\delta,u_i)\ge\theta(0,u_j)$. Consequently every nonzero coefficient of $\operatorname{adj}(A)_{ij}$ satisfies the required bound. No strict comparison or distinctness of weights has been used; all subtractions took place in $G$, not in truncated natural-number arithmetic.

proof.text: By the product formula in [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], a nonzero coefficient $[W^\delta]B_{ij}=[W^\delta](h\operatorname{adj}(A)_{ij})$ has a nonzero summand $[W^\epsilon]h\,[W^\eta]\operatorname{adj}(A)_{ij}$ with $\epsilon+\eta=\delta$. Step 4 gives $\theta(\eta,u_i)\ge\theta(0,u_j)$, and step 1 gives $\theta(\epsilon,0)\ge0$. Adding yields $\theta(\delta,u_i)\ge\theta(0,u_j)$, exactly the claimed inequality for $B=A^{-1}$. This uses no support restriction on the scalar inverse $h$.

proof.text: For $r=0$ there is just one empty matrix and no entry to test. Its determinant is $1$ by [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]; its product with itself is the empty identity, so the inverse assertion and the support assertion hold. For $m=0$, [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] identifies $R$ with $L$ and the only exponent is $0$; the same cofactor sums and cancellations still apply. For $n=0$, every weight is the empty vector and the support condition is automatic. The $r=1$ empty cofactor was included in step 3, and repeated weights were included in step 4.
